example.title: Finding an Unknown Quantity Using Complementary Angles
example.explanation:
From the diagram, we have 
\[
m\angle AOC=x + 24^{\circ}
\]
and 
\[
m\angle COD=3x.
\]  

Since [math]\angle AOC[/math] is complementary to [math]\angle COD,[/math] we have:

\begin{align*}
    (x + 24^{\circ}) + 3x &= 90^{\circ} \\[5pt]
    4x+24^{\circ} &= 90^\circ \\[5pt]
    4x&= 66^{\circ} \\[5pt]
    x&= 16.5^{\circ}
\end{align*}

example.title: Solving Multi-Step Problems Involving Complementary Angles
example.explanation:
Since [math]\angle AOC[/math] and [math]\angle COB[/math] are complementary angles, we have:

\begin{align}
m \angle AOC + m \angle COB & = 90^\circ \\[5pt]
m \angle AOC + 50^\circ & = 90^\circ \\[5pt]
m \angle AOC & = 40^\circ
\end{align}

Now, since [math]\angle AOC \cong \angle BOD,[/math] we have

\[m \angle BOD = m \angle AOC=40^\circ .\]

Therefore,

\begin{align}
m \angle AOD & =  m \angle AOC +m \angle COB+  m \angle BOD \\[5pt]
& = 40^\circ+50^\circ+40^\circ \\[5pt]
& = 130^\circ.
\end{align}
